newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee approves 19th century voting law.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee approves 19th century voting law.

text.p: Tennessee became the final state to pass the 15th Amendment to the Constitution guaranteeing the right to vote regardless of "race, colour or previous condition of servitude," 127 years after it became law.

In largely ceremonial vote on Wednesday, Tennessee legislators approved the amendment by a 98-0 vote in the state House and a 31-0 vote in the state Senate. The amendment, proposed after the Civil War to guarantee the right to vote to freed slaves, was originally ratified March 30, 1870 by three-quarters of the 37 states then in existence.
But Tennessee was not one of them and a 16-member black caucus in the state legislature decided to raise the issue a few weeks ago after a constitutional scholar brought it to their attention.

"I would like to say is that each of us is double privileged," Democratic State Representative Tommie Brown said prior to the vote. "First, we have the privilege of serving in this historic 100th general assembly, and we have the privilege of placing our print on history again by post-ratifying the 15th Amendment."
Neighbouring Kentucky was the last state to ratify the amendment prior to Tennessee, approving it in 1976.
